name: Naomi Tate
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember watching an audience from the kitchen hatch.” People around the public end of the South Shore boardwalk know Naomi by a small Thursday habit. Naomi checks the shade on the benches before deciding how long to stay.
voice: I came straight from a kitchen shift expecting a quick song. They gave me a whole uneven, wonderful play.
appearance: Naomi has brown hair pinned away from the temples, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a square of clean cloth for polishing smudges. When somebody else has the floor, Naomi steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Naomi thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Naomi sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To see the complete play straight from work.
family: Teresa Arendt is Naomi’s cousin raised in the same household. Naomi chooses the music. Teresa puts the kettle on. The cups come out before either brings up the reason for the visit. They trust a difficult conversation more if it has had an ordinary beginning. Asked about *The returned daughter*, Teresa says, “I agreed to fix the banister. Nobody asked me to mend the whole family and I won't promise it.”
connections: Alvin Jeong (child). The youth player gets to sing the line to the parent who finally knows what the rehearsal was for.
